newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers higher to steady.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers higher to steady.

text.p: North American bunker prices were higher to steady from prices earlier this week, refusing to follow the path of plunging NYMEX futures, traders said Thursday.
Earlier this week, bunkers largely slipped down on the threat of a tropical storm in the Gulf that failed to materialize in force.
On Thursday, New York Harbor 380 CST retraced, rising $5 to between $143 and $145 a tonne from prices last Tuesday.
"New York is tight on supply and will probably stay that way for awhile," said one East Coast player.
Harbor 180 CST also rose about $8 to $148/150, ignoring weak NYMEX heating oil futures, which the harbor has sometimes followed.
"It must be pretty tight if the Harbor is bearing the plunge of NYMEX," said a trader. NYMEX November heating oil ended off 3.05 cents at 70.92 cents a gallon.
In Houston, values stayed steady despite tight supply levels, with 380 CST trading $134/135 and 180 CST trading $137/138.
On the West Coast, traders said demand levels have been moderate, making for stable trade.

"There's a lot of business opportunity out there but no one is panicking," said one West Coast trader. "But if the Merc continues to drop, say another 75 cents tomorrow, then we are going to see a rundown."
Los Angeles 380 CST traded Thursday at $120/121.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1631
